To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we measured the two-particle correlation functions in the central rapidity region of p p collisions at the ISR and that the data show the existence of short-range positive correlation between secondaries within a region of about 2.5 units in η.
1) the two-particle correlation function exhibits short-range positive correlations between secondaries in the central region, and 2) these correlations are independent of the ISR energy.
the two-particle rapidities correlations in the ISR data are positive and short range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure of the hadronization process.
the study of the properties of the hadronic final state in high energy collisions.
the study of multiparticle correlations and their relation to the underlying dynamics of the particle production process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ISR results are consistent with the hypothesis that there exists a single source of particles, which has a finite size and which is located in the central region.
the ISR data are consistent with the assumption that the short-range correlations are the same at 23 and 63 GeV.
the data are in agreement with the hypothesis that the observed correlations are due to the production of a few particles in a small rapidity interval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the data show the existence of two-particle correlations that are consistent with a simple picture of the collision process in which the particles are produced in a common rapidity interval, but with a distribution of transverse momenta.

the data are consistent with an energy-independent, two-particle correlation function that is positive and short-range in the central region, with a diffractive component in the forward and backward regions.
, within the central region, the two-particle correlations are energy independent and are consistent with the hypothesis of independent particle production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that it is possible to extract the diffractive component from the inclusive two-particle correlations.

we have shown that the two-particle rapidities correlations are energy independent, which implies that the energy dependence of the multiplicity distribution is not due to the energy dependence of two-particle correlations.
the short-range correlations in multiparticle production are not a simple function of the energy of the colliding system.
